faq.a: Aasiyyah represents the traditional name form آسية (Āsiyah). Its exact lexical etymology is not established here; “living water” is not treated as verified.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aasiyyah?
faq.a: The recorded form آسية is associated with the traditional name Āsiyah in Islamic tradition.
The form is recorded in Arabic script, but this record does not assert a settled dictionary etymology for the personal name.

faq.q: What is the root of Aasiyyah?
faq.a: No root analysis is asserted because the exact etymology is not established in this record.
Aasiyyah is associated with Islamic tradition through Āsiyah, traditionally identified as Pharaoh's believing wife; this is separate from a literal name meaning.
This record does not establish آسية as an explicit Qur'anic personal name. The association with Pharaoh's wife is part of Islamic tradition.

faq.q: What does Aasiyyah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu it is written آسیہ. The earlier gloss “بہتا پانی، چشمہ، آبِ حیات” is not supported here and has been removed.
The supplied “aa-siy-yah” is approximate; the traditional form is commonly rendered Āsiyah.

faq.q: Is Aasiyyah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies this as feminine, consistent with traditional naming usage; regional frequency data is not provided.
